unit: one benchmark query of the join-tree rewriting suite, replayed fresh on the candidate plan and the paired reference plan. Development is the 20 public (dev) queries; the graded suite is all 39 (20 dev + 19 final) queries.

metrics.name: exact_result
metrics.means: 1 when the candidate plan returns the exact original query result for this query
metrics.source: judge/query_measurements.py compare_query exact equality; summarize_queries reports it per query as beat_spec_workload_passes[].metrics.exact_result
metrics.clears_when: candidate exact_result is true for this query
metrics.tolerance: none. Exact result equality per query.

metrics.name: median_latency
metrics.means: the candidate plan's fresh median execution latency for this query (DataFusion collect duration)
metrics.source: judge/query_measurements.py measured per-query medians, compared to the paired reference median; summarize_queries reports it per query as beat_spec_workload_passes[].metrics.median_latency
metrics.clears_when: candidate median latency < reference median latency for this query; a byte-identical reproduction of the reference plan automatically fails this comparison
metrics.tolerance: none. Strict below the fresh reference median; equality fails.

beats_reference: beats_reference = 1 iff every expected query clears both exact_result (true) and median_latency (candidate median strictly below reference median); otherwise 0. Missing measurements fail the verdict. The continuous average score is separate and returned regardless.

solver_feedback.name: all_metrics_progress
solver_feedback.means: how many of the evaluated train queries the candidate clears on both exact_result and median_latency, as passed, failed and total counts with pass_percent and fail_percent
solver_feedback.reveals_reference: no — it is one count over the 20 train queries of comparison outcomes the per-metric counts already summarize; it carries no query identity or ordering and no reference latency, ratio or margin. A count against a withheld reference tells how many queries the candidate currently wins, not which ones or by how much.

solver_feedback.name: candidate_median_latency_us
solver_feedback.means: the median, over the 20 train queries, of the candidate's own per-query median execution latency in microseconds; null unless every train query was measured
solver_feedback.reveals_reference: no — a single scalar computed only from the candidate's own measured latencies, with no reference or binary-baseline measurement, ratio, query identity or per-query value

withheld: query identities and ordering attached to any decision or measurement
statement_sentences: A separate all-query beats-reference verdict is evaluated beside the continuous average score. Every expected query must return the exact original result (exact_result) and run with a fresh median latency strictly below the paired reference median (median_latency); a byte-identical copy of the reference plan fails the latency comparison, and one failing query fails the verdict while the continuous score is still returned. Development (train) feedback returns the continuous score, aggregate beat_spec_progress with passed, failed, total, pass_percent and fail_percent for each of the two comparisons over the 20 train queries, all_metrics_progress with the same fields for queries clearing both comparisons, and candidate_median_latency_us, the median of the candidate's own per-query median latencies. Query identities, per-query decisions and latencies, reference values, ratios and margins are not returned, and final evaluation returns no solver-visible metrics.
comments: The spec transcribes the verdict that judge/query_measurements.py computes per query: exact_result AND fresh median latency strictly below the paired reference (byte-identical reference fails), conjoined over the complete 20/39 expected query set. summarize_queries emits the per-query decisions as beat_spec_workload_passes and the two solver_feedback aggregates (all_metrics_progress over the whole suite, candidate_median_latency_us null unless every query was measured); the shared verifier (tasks/shared/verifier) turns the decisions into aggregate train beat_spec_progress and the private final verdict. Before the task.toml migration the task's own verifier adapter did that conversion and its private final verdict listed each query's decisions; the decisions now stay in evidence (metrics.queries) and the private verdict is the shared per-metric aggregate. Leakage review: a rewrite policy sees each query's join tree and can treat queries differently, so a solver can attribute a pass count to one train query by making the others fail, at about one train call per attribution. That reveals whether a submitted plan beat the reference plan on that train query in that evaluation, not the reference's latency or plan; the 19 hidden final queries are never evaluated in train. candidate_median_latency_us is a median over all 20 queries and is null when any query is unmeasured, so isolating one query does not turn it into that query's latency. The full version of the paper (Appendix D, Table 2 / Fig. 13) additionally reports join-only runtime; the task measures total plan execution latency only, so join-only time is out of scope and would require operator-level timing in a separate release.
